blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Supreme Court of India functions under defined constitutional provisions governing its composition, appointments, tenure, and independence.
Article 131 outlines the Original Jurisdiction of the Supreme Court to adjudicate disputes between the Centre and States or among States.
Article 32 guarantees Writ Jurisdiction for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights.
Article 136 provides discretionary power via Special Leave Petitions against any judgment or order.
Article 142 authorizes the Court to issue decrees or orders necessary to deliver complete justice.
Article 143 empowers the President to consult the Supreme Court under Advisory Jurisdiction.

blocks.content: The Supreme Court of India is the highest judicial authority of the country and the final interpreter of the Constitution.
It is the guardian of the Constitution and protector of Fundamental Rights.
The Supreme Court ensures justice, maintains the supremacy of the Constitution, and settles disputes between:

items:
• Centre and States
  • States and States
  • Citizens and Government

blocks.content: The provisions related to the Supreme Court are mentioned in Part V (Articles 124–147) of the Indian Constitution.

blocks.content: Parliament has the power to increase the number of judges.
Judges of the Supreme Court are appointed by the President of India. Appointment is done through the Collegium System:

items:
• Chief Justice of India
  • Four senior-most judges of SC

blocks.content: This system ensures independence of judiciary.
To become a judge of Supreme Court:

items:
• Must be citizen of India
  • Must have been a High Court judge for 5 years OR
  • Advocate of High Court for 10 years OR
  • Distinguished jurist in opinion of President
Must have been a High Court judge for 5 years OR
Advocate of High Court for 10 years OR
Distinguished jurist in opinion of President
• Judge holds office till 65 years of age
Judge holds office till 65 years of age

• By impeachment
  • Proven misbehavior or incapacity
  • Special majority in Parliament

• Salary charged from Consolidated Fund of India
  • Cannot be reduced during tenure
  • Ensures independence of judiciary
Salary charged from Consolidated Fund of India

blocks.content: The Supreme Court has five types of jurisdiction:
Original jurisdiction means cases that can be directly filed in Supreme Court. Includes:

items:
• Disputes between Centre and States
  • Disputes between two or more States
  • Federal disputes
Disputes between two or more States

blocks.content: Article 136 gives Supreme Court discretionary power to grant Special Leave to Appeal.

rows: Article 226 (Wider scope: Fundamental and other legal rights)

items:
• Can be filed against any court or tribunal
  • Not a matter of right
  • Most powerful jurisdiction of SC
Can be filed against any court or tribunal

Article 32 is called the “Heart and Soul of the Constitution” by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.
The President may seek opinion of Supreme Court on:

items:
• Questions of law
  • Questions of public importance Opinion is not binding but respected.
Questions of public importance Opinion is not binding but respected.

blocks.content: Supreme Court is a Court of Record. It means:

items:
• Its judgments are preserved
  • Can punish for contempt of court
Can punish for contempt of court

blocks.content: Judicial Review allows the Supreme Court to:

items:
• Examine constitutionality of laws
  • Strike down unconstitutional laws
  • Protect Fundamental Rights

blocks.content: Article 142 empowers Supreme Court to pass any order necessary to do complete justice.
This power is unique and extraordinary.

items: Article 32 is specifically designated for enforcing Fundamental Rights and is directly accessible by citizens.
Article 136 Special Leave Petitions are a discretionary remedy and cannot be claimed as a matter of right.
Advisory opinions given under Article 143 are not binding on the President.
Article 129 empowers the Supreme Court as a Court of Record with the authority to punish for contempt of itself.

blocks.content: The Supreme Court is the guardian of the Constitution and the final protector of citizens’ rights.
It ensures justice, liberty, equality, and rule of law in India.
Without the Supreme Court, democracy cannot function effectively.
